column1: Lili is the fashionista dancing diva of Tekken 8 and her gameplay shows this off with extremely long range tools that allow her to play her preferred distance which is the mid-range. Moves like "df3+4" and "ss4" are slower linear mids that reach the opponent from quite far, allowing her to fish for combos while setting up fast backturn pressure ("BT d+2" and "BT 3") keeping the opponent guessing. She balances these with "3+4" and "d3" which both track really well, making sure that the opponent plays into her game instead of sidestepping away from her pressure.
Lili is very much a beginner-friendly character
column2: having a simple yet effective game plan that balances keepout and lockdown. She can feel a little tricky to pilot at times since most of her strong moves are slow and can get counter hit or floated out of her approach tools
column3: but she generally is not execution heavy. Her 50/50s are very strong but require committing to set-ups such as staying in her backturn stance or jumping into Feisty Rabbit.

column1: One of the most toxic wake up situations in the game while Heat is active (Feisty Rabbit, "b3" or "b4").

Lili has really strong stand-alone moves as she typically does not rely on string pressure and offense. Her mids like "df3", "f4" and "f3" tend to be quite chunky while her lows like "d3" and "d1,2" tend to be annoying to deal with.

She is generally a very versatile character and can be played, simple, slow and patient, baiting whiffs with her movement or lockdown heavy with her plus frames ("df3" , "qcf3+4", "ff4b") and long range approach tools ("ss4", "df3+4", "3+4", "d3").
Lili's tracking is generally her biggest weakness. A lot of her key pressure moves can be stepped easily.
Most of Lili's key moves revolve around the 20 frame mark which tends to make her feel slow.
This makes her fairly easy to interrupt and counter hit launch with fast moves.

Lili's main Heat mechanic relies on setting up her Feisty Rabbit stance ("b3" or "b4"), bunny hopping around the opponent to create dangerous 50/50 mix ups on their wake-up or after massive plus frames. As well as this, she gets to recover Heat Bar if she commits to a double jump by holding "b3" or "b4".

She also gets to chip the opponent down with enhanced versions of her "ff3+4" move and all its variations ( "qcf1,4" , "1,2,4" ,  "b4,4" and "b3,4"). All of these become +5 on block as of season 3, giving her a bit more advantage to play around the oppoenent and set up her slower offense.

As of Season 3, Lili's Feisty Rabbit as well as Heat pressure have received nerfs when it comes to timer consumption and with the removal of heat recovery, you need to be more careful and more deliberate with her mix-ups. This gives a little more variety to her gameplan in heat since prior to the update all she could rely on safely for mix-up potential was the Feisty 50-50 which she can perform a Heat Burst or a Heat Smash from also. Having access to "3+4,3+4" in heat giving her a +7 opportunity in backturn as well as her neutral Heatsmash which goes into Dew Glide at +14 when holding forward, makes her offense a lot more dangerous and diverse, while still having the threat of an unseeable and unparryable low backturn Heat Smash if you position yourself for it.
